Definition: a primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose):--kill, (do) sacrifice, slay.
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, thýō means to sacrifice, to slay. In Matthew 22:4, Again, he sent forth other servants. Across its 13 occurrences, the word keeps that same sense, whether the setting is promise or warning.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that sacrifice in Scripture always costs something, because what is offered to God is never leftovers. That is why I read the passages around thýō slowly, instead of hurrying past.
